To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

random sampling of patches from an image, with a fixed sampling rate, gives better performance than interest operators, and that the number of patches per image is the most important parameter governing performance.

for a given descriptor and codebook, random sampling of patches gives equal or better classification results than multiscale interest operators, and that the number of samples is by far the most important factor governing classification performance.

for bag-of-features image classification: (1) the best sampling method is random, (2) the number of samples is the most important factor governing classification accuracy and (3) the best codebook creation method is K-means.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to sample patches from the image for bag-of-features image representation and classification.
the practical implementation issues that arise in the design of a bag-of-features system.
the sampling of image patches for bag-of-features image classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important factor in the design of a bag-of-features image classifier is the number of samples taken from each test image.
the best bag-of-features image classifiers use a large number of randomly sampled patches and a simple normalized histogram of local features as the characterization of the image.
random sampling is a viable and effective method for bag-of-features image classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for image classification, random sampling of patches from the test image gives equal or better results than the state of the art multiscale interest operators, and the best classifiers can be obtained by combining random and multiscale interest operators.

for a given number of samples, a random sampling scheme is as good as any other, but for a given number and size of codebook, the best sampling strategy is to sample the maximum number of patches possible.
the bag-of-features approach is a very flexible and robust image classification framework, and that it is not necessary to use complex interest operators to obtain good performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
random sampling is a viable and competitive alternative to multiscale interest operators for bag-of-features image classification.

the choice of sampling method is more important than the choice of interest operator and that for large numbers of samples random sampling gives better results than the commonly used multiscale interest operators.
random sampling of patches is a simple and effective way to build a bag-of-features image classifier.
